question: A marketer's long-running chat has begun producing copy that ignores the campaign brief agreed weeks earlier. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Open a fresh chat; check whether the old chat had grown too long; paste the brief in; capture the decisions afterwards.
B) Capture the decisions; open a fresh chat; check whether the old chat had grown too long; paste the brief in afterwards.
C) Check whether the chat has simply grown too long; capture the brief and decisions; open a fresh chat; paste them in there.
D) Paste the brief in again; capture the decisions; check whether the chat has grown too long; open a fresh chat right at the end.
correct_answers: C) Check whether the chat has simply grown too long; capture the brief and decisions; open a fresh chat; paste them in there.
explanations: Incorrect. Restarting before capturing the decisions risks losing them, and diagnosing after the fact wastes the step.
Incorrect. Working in the new chat before the brief is in place produces exactly the drift she is trying to fix.
Correct. Diagnosing the cause comes before acting, capturing the durable material protects it, and only then is restarting safe rather than destructive.
Incorrect. Re-pasting into an already overloaded conversation adds pressure to the window before anything has been diagnosed.
